source.title: Exploring the Search Space of Neural Network Combinations obtained with Efficient Model Stitching
source.authors: A. Guijt; D. Thierens; T. Alderliesten; Peter A. N. Bosman

record.tranche_reason: The study uses learned stitching layers to connect representations from pretrained networks and reports how well the resulting subnetworks perform. This tests stitch-based interchangeability, but it does not directly measure representational similarity.
record.gate_note: The relevant results are the reported performance of evolved stitched subnetworks relative to parent networks and their ensemble. The paper discusses representational mismatch as motivation, but reports no direct similarity score. Numeric coordinates in Figures 4–5 are not transcribed here; hypervolume comparisons between search algorithms are not results about stitching interchangeability.
record.test_reason: The paper uses model stitching, with linear or 1x1-conv layers trained by local MSE, as a recombination operator for neuroevolution. Its results are Pareto fronts (accuracy vs multiply-adds) of subnetworks chosen by evolutionary search, compared with the parents and their ensemble, plus hypervolume comparisons between search algorithms. It reports no per-stitch or per-layer loss when one network's representation is mapped onto another's, and no unselected stitching performance. So it measures its own method's search performance, not how interchangeable the representations are (V4).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that stitching lets two pretrained networks be recombined, without training each offspring, into functional offspring with new accuracy–cost trade-offs that sometimes dominate a parent or the ensemble. They also note that validation gains for cheaper networks largely vanish on the test set and that the cheapest parent is never dominated.
record.recipe_differences: Uses model stitching with trainable linear or linear-like connector layers, but matches layers across network graphs and trains all stitches together using local MSE targets rather than the original approach's separate task-specific training procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported trade-off differs across network pairs and tasks. The authors also state that the layer-matching approach affects the distribution of available computational costs; they do not report a controlled comparison of alternative similarity measures or matching procedures.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors state that stitches may not fully perform the transformation and that their errors compound. With uniformly sampled stitches, networks often become nonfunctional, so initialization is biased to about 6 stitches. Cheap, many-stitch networks reach only 0.10–0.30 accuracy on ImageNet (a). This is qualitative or from preliminary experiments, with no controlled measure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear stitching errors accumulate when many stitches are chained, so multi-stitch recombinations of different-architecture CNNs lose much performance.

record.problems: The paper evaluates only a small set of vision-model pairs and tasks. Evaluation uses the first 1000 ImageNet validation samples and first 64 VOC validation samples during search. The claimed performance trade-offs are largely described qualitatively in the text or shown in plots; detailed results are referred to as supplementary material.
record.rows_left_out: Figure-only numeric coordinates from Figures 4–5 were not extracted because the supplied text does not state them numerically. Table 1 hypervolume values were left out because they compare search algorithms rather than directly measuring stitch-based interchangeability.

untested.parts: Not tested: convergence with scale or capability.
No direct measure of stitching loss or mapping quality between layers. Only search-selected subnetwork fronts are reported.
Not tested: universal features or circuits.
Not tested: dependence on the similarity measure, its settings or the inputs.
Not tested: partial or plateauing alignment, or its causes.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked all rows to V4. However, the rows are outputs of a multi-objective search optimized on small validation subsets: 1000 ImageNetV2 samples and 64 VOC samples. Many of the dominating networks are partial ensembles with shared layers. These results do not measure how losslessly one model's representation maps onto another's, so this is treated as T4 use of stitching as a tool.

versions.untested_parts: Scale- and capability-dependent convergence across independently trained models.
Vision-language alignment on paired images and captions as model capability changes.
Convergence across random seeds, features, or shared subspaces.

The study tests stitch-based connections between pretrained vision networks on classification and segmentation tasks. It does not test cross-modal mappings, relative representations, unpaired-data mappings, or broad interchangeability across arbitrary models.
Recurrence of interpretable features or circuits across models.
Dependence of measured representational convergence on similarity metrics, their settings, or input distributions.
Whether representational alignment plateaus or is caused by shared data or objectives.

rows.subject: resnet152 and efficientnet_b4 stitched subnetworks
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate evolved subnetworks using trained stitching layers against parent networks and their ensemble.
rows.measure: Accuracy and multiply-add computational cost trade-off
rows.baseline: The parent networks and their ensemble, referred to as reference networks
rows.value: The search found stitched networks that dominated the other parent network and the ensemble.
rows.note: The result is stated qualitatively; the plotted front is not assigned numerical coordinates here.
rows.check: Selection value: these are the best subnetworks found by optimizing on the validation set. Dominating a parent reflects search plus ensembling with shared layers, not stitching loss. It cannot show how much is lost when representations are mapped.

rows.subject: deeplabv3_mobilenet_v3_large and deeplabv3_resnet50 stitched subnetworks
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate evolved subnetworks using trained stitching layers against parent networks and their ensemble.
rows.measure: Accuracy and multiply-add computational cost trade-off
rows.baseline: The parent networks and their ensemble, referred to as reference networks
rows.value: The search found stitched networks that dominated the other parent network and the ensemble.
rows.note: The result is stated qualitatively; the plotted front is not assigned numerical coordinates here.
rows.check: Selection value from the search on the validation set, as in r1. The front mixes ensembles with stitched paths, so stitching loss cannot be read from it.

rows.subject: resnet50 and resnext50_32x4d stitched subnetworks
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate evolved subnetworks using trained stitching layers against parent networks and their ensemble.
rows.measure: Accuracy and multiply-add computational cost trade-off
rows.baseline: The parent networks and their ensemble, referred to as reference networks
rows.value: Finding an improvement that dominates either parent is described as difficult, particularly because the parents have similar computational cost and leave little room to reduce cost while retaining high performance.
rows.note: The paper reports a qualitative limitation rather than a numerical result for this comparison.
rows.check: The difficulty of dominating a parent is attributed to the parents' similar computational cost, not to stitch quality. This is a search-space property of the method.

rows.subject: resnet152 and efficientnet_b4 stitched subnetworks
rows.operation_detail: Re-evaluate evolved subnetworks from the approximation front against parent networks and their ensemble.
rows.measure: Accuracy and multiply-add computational cost trade-off
rows.baseline: The parent networks and their ensemble, referred to as reference networks
rows.value: Accuracy improvements for cheaper networks appeared to disappear on the test set, while more expensive networks generalized; one parent remained dominated, but the gap to the reference networks had shrunk considerably.
rows.note: The paper describes this test-set pattern across the fronts and notes the ImageNet (a) parent that remains dominated.
rows.check: Test-set re-evaluation of validation-selected fronts. It shows overfitting of the search, not representational mapping quality.

rows.subject: resnet50 and resnext50_32x4d stitched subnetworks
rows.operation_detail: Re-evaluate evolved subnetworks from the approximation front against parent networks and their ensemble.
rows.measure: Accuracy and multiply-add computational cost trade-off
rows.baseline: The parent networks and their ensemble, referred to as reference networks
rows.value: The paper reports that accuracy gains for cheaper networks generally disappeared on test evaluation, while more expensive networks generalized; the gap to reference networks shrank considerably.
rows.note: This is the paper's general description of test-set re-evaluation applied to this task's front.
rows.check: The paper states the test-set pattern generally, not specifically for ImageNet (b). It is a test of search generalization, not of interchangeability.

rows.subject: deeplabv3_mobilenet_v3_large and deeplabv3_resnet50 stitched subnetworks
rows.operation_detail: Re-evaluate evolved subnetworks from the approximation front against parent networks and their ensemble.
rows.measure: Accuracy and multiply-add computational cost trade-off
rows.baseline: The parent networks and their ensemble, referred to as reference networks
rows.value: Accuracy improvements for cheaper networks appeared to disappear on the test set, while more expensive networks generalized; a parent and the ensemble remained dominated, but the gap to the reference networks had shrunk considerably.
rows.note: The paper states that a parent and ensemble for VOC remain dominated on test evaluation, with a substantially smaller gap.
rows.check: Test-set re-evaluation of the search front, as in r4. It does not measure mapping loss.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Stitched subnetworks were reported to dominate a parent network and the ensemble on the validation fronts, showing useful stitch-based interchangeability in these settings (r1, r2).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: ImageNet (b) validation and test-set evaluations across the reported tasks
reader_labels.reason: Dominating parents was difficult for the similar-cost ImageNet (b) pair, and the cheaper networks' accuracy gains generally did not carry over to test evaluation, although more expensive networks generalized (r3, r4, r5, r6).
